title: Gaussian limit for normalized Boolean blocks
statement: Let $n\ge0$ and let $F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ be bounded and continuous. For each $m\ge0$, take independent uniform signs $\varepsilon_{ij}\in\{-1,1\}$, with $1\le i\le n$ and $1\le j\le m+1$, and set $S_m(i)=(m+1)^{-1/2}\sum_{j=1}^{m+1}\varepsilon_{ij}$. Then $\mathbb E[F(S_m)]\to\int F\,d\gamma_n$ as $m\to\infty$, where $\gamma_n$ is standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$.
hypotheses_covered: $F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ is bounded and continuous
replaced: Let $\gamma_n$ be standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$. For independent uniform bits $X_{ij}$, put $S_r(X)_i=r^{-1/2}\sum_{j=1}^r(-1)^{X_{ij}}$. For every $n\ge0$ and bounded continuous $F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$, $\mathbb E F(S_{m+1}(X))\to\int F\,d\gamma_n$ as $m\to\infty$.
